scope: RETAINED NEGATIVE establishing a boundary, not a pad-level verdict: reaching a pad's IOMUX terminal in the routed netlist with a valid feeder is NOT sufficient for that pad to drive on silicon. observed: Decoded all 66 pad approach chains from the vendor build that routes all 33 L48 pads simultaneously (padmap_full_20260814/logic_db/route.tx) and compared, per top-edge pad, the feeder RMUX that agamemnon/chipdb/padfeed_L48_top.csv offers against the feeder the vendor actually drives into that pad's IOMUX. They agree for exactly ONE pad of ten: PIN_18 (18,13,z0) RMUX28. The nine disagreements are PIN_19 ours RMUX8 vs vendor RMUX16; PIN_17 RMUX20 vs RMUX16; PIN_16 {RMUX0,4,8,16,24} vs RMUX12; PIN_15 RMUX16 vs RMUX28; PIN_14 RMUX0 vs RMUX24; PIN_13 RMUX12 vs RMUX8; PIN_10 RMUX24 vs RMUX8; PIN_11 RMUX28 vs RMUX4; PIN_12 RMUX20 vs RMUX0.
scope: Data defect located in padfeed_L48_top.csv, explaining a standing silicon observation rather than adding a claim. PIN_18 -- the single top-edge pad that has ever driven on silicon -- is the single pad whose shipped feeder matches the vendor's. The other nine route to their IOMUX terminal and configure, but drive nothing, consistent with our table pointing the router at a different physical approach than the silicon uses. This does NOT establish that the nine pads will work once corrected; it identifies the correction to make and the prediction to test. No feature claim changes.

consequence: The pad enable pattern is EXACT, not monotone, and there is no safe superset. io_emit already recorded that OMITTING bits leaves the pad static; this shows ADDING them does too, with the image still valid and accepted. That kills the obvious shortcut for the uncharacterized pad-slot sets -- 'just enable every block' produces a config-accepted image with a dead pin. io_emit.emit_sels() therefore now FAILS CLOSED on an unlisted slot set instead of its old ENABLE.get(active, {}), which emitted the source-select alone and left the pin dead with nothing reported. Six of the fifteen non-empty slot sets are characterized; the rest are now a build error rather than a silent failure.
next_experiment: Harvest the missing slot-set patterns from vendor builds. The corpus scan (174 routed vendor designs, tools/agamemnon/engine_work/harvest_pad_enable.py) found only 19 that drive a ring pad, and the analytic shortcut of classifying sel %% 7 == 6 as an enable bit is WRONG -- those bits are all over the idle frames, which is why a first pass reported 2,948 of 3,327 tile observations as pad configuration on tiles with no pad. Either build one vendor oracle per slot set, or diff against a same-tile idle image from the same design family.
observed: Silicon A/B on the ring-pad CFG_IOMUX enable bits. Baseline: the known-good PIN_18 image (pin18_toggle_uncomp.bin) FCB-accepts 0x000f0002 and toggles at 460,856 Hz on Pico GP8 (27,173 edges in a 29.5 ms window). Patched: the same image with six enable bits ADDED at the (17,13) config tile so every block of banks 0-3 is set (CFG_IOMUX0 sels 6 and 34, CFG_IOMUX1 sels 20 and 27, CFG_IOMUX2 sels 6 and 13), CRC recomputed, sha256 e7f4efe1918fdb3811f921a4011f3b7c3f4c9c233654feb63dc70018e6a1e4ec. It still FCB-accepts 0x000f0002 and the pad reads ZERO edges.
scope: One pad (PIN_18 z0 on the (18,13) tile), one direction of perturbation. It does NOT characterize any new slot set and adds no pad capability -- it removes a silent-failure mode and rules out a shortcut. The qualified pad surface is unchanged.

consequence: Un-blames the observation channel. The 2026-08-15 X15 carry-seam pad campaign recorded NO verdict because all three images AND the no-carry sanity control read zero edges on GP8, and a control that cannot drive the pin makes the carry readings meaningless. The channel itself is fine, so that failure belongs to the pad BUILD path in that campaign, not to the rig or the wiring. Re-run those seams with a pad build whose slot set is characterized -- or read them over the MCU exit, which is working.
next_experiment: Re-run the X15 seam pad readouts now that emit_sels fails closed: if that campaign's builds used an uncharacterized slot set, they will now refuse to build instead of producing a silently dead pin.
observed: The known-good PIN_18 toggle image loaded via pad_read_run.py reads 27,173 edges / 460,856 Hz on Pico GP8.
scope: Channel health check only. No feature claim.

consequence: The pad-slot ENABLE lookup is retired as a model. It held six of fifteen sets and the other nine could not be driven at all; there is now a closed-form rule covering every set, at any tile, with no table to outgrow. It also fixes a latent bug the table hid: the flat 7*z + ... source-select form runs off the end of bank 0 for index >= 6, which is reachable on the wider left-edge tiles (up to z11). io_emit.index_config() is the measured form and io_emit.slot_config() the narrower open-flow form the qualified PIN_18 image uses; they are deliberately separate functions, because validating one against the other's ground truth is how a plausible rule gets confirmed against the wrong thing.
next_experiment: Drive a previously impossible slot set on silicon end to end -- two or more slots on one top-edge tile through the open flow -- and read both pads on the Pico.
observed: Fifteen af.exe oracles were built, one per non-empty subset of the pad slots {0,1,2,3} on IOTILE (19,13) (z0=PIN_16, z1=PIN_15, z2=PIN_14, z3=PIN_13), plus a no-pad control from the identical flow. Differencing each against the control at the (18,13) config tile shows the CFG_IOMUX bits are NOT a per-set pattern. Every IOMUX index parks at 7*block + 6; driving an index UNPARKS it and writes two source-select bits; a pad slot z occupies TWO indices, z and z+4; and index i lives at bank, block = divmod(i, 6). That rule reproduces all fifteen builds EXACTLY -- every set bit and every clear bit, 15/15, with no residual. Our own from-scratch base frame is byte-identical to the vendor control at that tile (24 park bits set, nothing else), so the deltas apply directly.
scope: Decode of vendor builds plus our own base frame; the fifteen measurements are at one config tile, (18,13), serving pad tile (19,13). It does NOT by itself qualify any new pad on silicon and adds no pad to the qualified surface. The corpus ships as chipdb/pad_iomux_slotset_L48.csv and tests/test_pad_iomux_slotset.py requires the rule to reproduce every row.

consequence: The park bits are per-block and independent: only the blocks belonging to a driven index matter, and unparking a spare block does not disturb a working pad. Together with the re-parking result this closes the model in both directions on silicon, which is what licenses applying the decoded rule to slot sets no vendor oracle covers. It also explains the earlier nine-pad failure without any appeal to the fabric: those images left driven blocks parked.
next_experiment: Build a two-slot open image on IOTILE (19,13) using the rule and confirm both pads toggle on the Pico.
observed: Second half of the silicon A/B on the known-good PIN_18 image, testing the other direction. Re-parking a DRIVEN block was already shown to kill the pad (460,856 Hz -> 0 edges). Here the park bits of an UNUSED slot were cleared instead: slot 1 occupies IOMUX indices 1 and 5, so CFG_IOMUX0 sels 13 and 41 at the (17,13) config tile were cleared and the CRC recomputed (sha256 358eecd2fa8322e80108f2584f636e9026f1d8538afb3573f80a39c4b9449816). FCB accepts 0x000f0002 and PIN_18 still toggles at 461,555 Hz (27,205 edges), unchanged within noise.
scope: One pad, one tile, two perturbations. It bounds the mechanism; it does not qualify a new pad or slot set.

consequence: Two things separate. (1) Every pad of every group image built before this was being asked to output a CONSTANT -- the flip-flop could not toggle -- so the whole nine-pad negative was measured on designs with no signal in them, and none of its pad-configuration conclusions were ever tested. (2) A multi-pad group image CAN drive a pad: the group flow is not the obstacle. What each pad still needs is its own forced conducting APPROACH chain plus the pad-feed hop codeword for the (source, destination RMUX) pair actually routed. PIN_18 has both; no other top pad has either, which is why it remains the only one that drives.
next_experiment: Force the vendor's approach for a (19,13) pad end to end. The oracles give it exactly: for PIN_16 the vendor routes UFMTILE(13,7):BufMUX8 -> InputMUX8 -> LogicTILE(15,7):RMUX62 -> LogicTILE(15,9):RMUX61 -> LogicTILE(19,9):RMUX55 -> IOTILE(19,13):RMUX8 -> IOMUX0. Note also that the vendor drives the z+4 twin index as a SEPARATE signal with its own feeder (IOMUX4 <- R16 from LogicTILE(19,11)) -- an output enable we never drive, only unpark. That difference is named but untested.
observed: The multi-pad group builder never called qin_pack.permute_selffb_to_pinC. A toggle FF's self-feedback has to ride the slice's dedicated feedback mux (pinC); routed as an ordinary OMUX->IMUX hop it has no encoding, and bitgen duly reported one 'UNMAPPED IMUXn <- OMUXm d=(0,0)' per flip-flop -- 4 of 32 pips in the (18,13) group, 3 of 23 in the (19,13) group. Adding the call takes the (18,13) group to 28 pips, 27 mapped, 0 unmapped. Then the control that should have been run first: build the group containing the ONE pad already known to drive. Without the proven approach forced, PIN_18 reads 0 edges through the group flow. With the single-pad flow's own approach blacklist and its FF tile, the same group image reads 425,005 edges / 424,101 Hz on Pico GP8 (image sha256 686bc07212212c37743d3158b18e28e8b5dde02bfc3d9e0f4b971c3a8b81f195). PIN_17, the second pad of that group, stays static.
scope: One pad driving in a two-pad image. It does NOT widen the qualified pad ring -- PIN_18 was already qualified -- and PIN_17, PIN_16, PIN_15, PIN_14 and PIN_13 all remain static. What it establishes is that the remaining blocker is per-pad approach and hop data, not the multi-pad flow, the IOMUX enable model, or the fabric.

consequence: Explains why padfeed_L48_top.csv only ever worked for PIN_18. Its (19,13) rows name a source at (19,12) while every vendor build feeds that tile from (19,9), and the codeword is source-dependent -- so the table pointed the mux at an input our design does not drive. Four vendor-sourced rows were added for (19,13). Separately, arch.py's pad-feed pip loader never consulted the edge blacklist, so a ban on a pad-feed edge silently did nothing and the router kept using the CSV's source tile; that is the same defect as the BRAM pip loader and is now fixed.
next_experiment: Promote the twelve harvested (source, destination) hop codewords as a chipdb table and emit them from padfeed, then re-read the (19,13) group.
observed: Extending the fifteen slot-set oracles beyond CFG_IOMUX recovers the pad-feed hop too -- the RMUX source-select at the config tile that puts a fabric net onto the pad tile's RMUX. It is a 2-hot pair in a CFG_RMUX group at (18,13), the group is destination R // 8, and the PAIR depends on the source: twelve (source@(19,9), destination R) combinations were observed, e.g. RMUX55->R8 = CFG_RMUX1(0,4), RMUX85->R16 = CFG_RMUX2(0,4), RMUX92->R28 = CFG_RMUX3(25,27), RMUX9->R12 = CFG_RMUX1(26,28). Source tile matters as well as source index: RMUX62@(19,11)->R16 gives (2,4) where RMUX85@(19,9)->R16 gives (0,4).
scope: Decode only, one config tile. No pad is qualified by this record. The codewords are applied by hand in the workbench today; they are not yet emitted by the flow.

It is NOT the ten-pad PIN_10..PIN_19 ring: the other eight pads have no silicon observation, no measured hop codeword for their composition, and are not in the qualified-composition table.

scope: Two pads, one package (L48), one profile. The build runs under the research-unsafe profile because the Python-architecture placer composes AGAMEMNON_SOFT_PREFER, AGAMEMNON_SOFT_PENALTY and AGAMEMNON_NO_FFBRIDGE, which are registered experimental. That gate is not specific to pads -- a plain non-pad toggle design is rejected by release-strict identically -- and no gate was loosened to obtain this result.

consequence: Each was a silent failure that presented as a clean build. The blacklist ones matter most: they are the mechanism the qualified-composition restriction relies on, so a pad rule that looked applied was not. tests/test_blacklist_covers_supplemental_pips.py now requires every ctx.addPip loop in the routing feature to consult the shared ban predicate.
next_experiment: None; covered by regression tests.
observed: Four production defects were found by driving the ordinary CLI at this design and are fixed. (1) Supplemental graph loaders ignored the edge blacklist -- the package pad-feed rows, the vendor RMUX-to-IOMUX terminal rows, the synthesized carry/OMUX/direct-D feedback pips, the admitted-IOTILE rows and the left-edge exact corridors -- so a ban on any of those edges silently did nothing. (2) The blacklist key was compared as a raw string, so RMUX8 and RMUX08 never matched. (3) chipdb_schema imported zlib at module scope, which nextpnr's embedded Python on Windows cannot load, killing the arch script before it read a wire. (4) The PCF placer left the clock IOB to the placer, which bound it to an output-only pad bel (bel X8Y0_OPAD3 has no pin O), and whether that happened depended on how many other IOBs the design had.
scope: Production flow repairs. No new silicon claim.

consequence: This supersedes the numbers in the earlier production record, which were measured before the final code path; the conclusion is unchanged and the earlier record stays as history. One more production defect was found getting here and is worth stating: routing.py builds its physical-PCF terminal whitelist (_PHYS_PAD_TERM) from iomux_hop_vendor.csv, so a pad with any hop row exposes ONLY those feeders. Removing the feeder-8 rows for PIN_16 -- done to stop a genuine feature-ownership collision, since the codeword now lives in padfeed_L48_top.csv -- silently removed the qualified terminal from the graph and the build stopped routing entirely. The row is restored with EMPTY set_cells: terminal exposure and codeword ownership are different jobs and one table was doing both.
next_experiment: Add a third pad to chipdb/pad_output_qualified_L48.csv and repeat the matrix against a neighbouring qualified pad.

All three built by the ordinary CLI, all FCB-accept 0x000f0002, all emit 0 unmapped, 0 predicted, 0 legacy-abs. BOTH (sha256 7924c41169fbaa4c30ade041aef9423a0a58c981a7a72997236434a39ab6bd6b, 33 pips): GP8 = 3,195,844 Hz (188,395 edges) and GP6 = 3,195,806 Hz (188,348 edges). PIN_18 ONLY (sha256 37f9e4325a41feda9d827979ae05f0d3da57e28f0c74d5492071be283852c3d1, 13 pips): GP8 = 3,193,698 Hz, GP6 = 0. PIN_16 ONLY (sha256 40309ef7095a11ff6bd3efdf6d5a0e77942e39633e6f76863281dc8696621f7f, 12 pips): GP8 = 0, GP6 = 3,197,832 Hz. Neighbouring pads GP7, GP2, GP5 and GP3 read 0 edges in all three. The retained routed netlist (routed sha256 b8916357bf141829a6e57c6bbef89449657ed3444379587189a3d45ccc911983) repacks byte-identically to the measured image from a clean CLI pack invocation.
scope: Two pads, L48, research-unsafe profile. The rates are higher than the earlier record because the ring form divides differently; the qualified claim is that each pad toggles and that the two are independent, not a specific frequency.

consequence: The qualified top-edge output surface is now exactly PIN_18, PIN_16 and PIN_15 -- three pads, still NOT the ten-pad PIN_10..PIN_19 ring. Two further results come with it. (1) A single-variable silicon discrimination of the pad-feed source: the SAME design routed through RMUX85@(19,11) instead of RMUX85@(19,9) config-accepted with 0 unmapped, emitted the measured codeword for that source (bytes 2491,2492), had correct IOMUX slot bits, and read a hard 0 Hz on GP2; the (19,9) build toggles. Same feeder RMUX16, same slot bits, same IOMUX terminal -- only the source and its codeword differ. This does not separate 'the (19,11) codeword row is mis-measured' from 'the (19,11) source does not conduct into this pad'; both remain open. (2) PIN_16 z0 and PIN_15 z1 share pad tile (19,13) AND config tile (18,13), with slot bits in neighbouring blocks of the same banks, and they drive together with no interference -- the strongest available check that the CFG_IOMUX park/unpark rule is exact rather than approximate.
next_experiment: PIN_14 (19,13 z2) is the next candidate by the same readiness ranking. It needs its pad-feed codeword confirmed for the source the router actually takes, then the same single-pad plus shared-tile-pair matrix. Separately: the (19,11) negative deserves a codeword re-measurement to tell a bad table row from a non-conducting source.
observed: PIN_15 (pad tile 19,13 slot z1, Pico GP2) is the THIRD qualified top-edge output pad. All images built by the ordinary CLI -- agamemnon build <source> --pcf <constraints> --research-unsafe -- with 0 unmapped, 0 predicted, 0 legacy-abs selectors, and all FCB-accept 0x000f0002. PAIR PIN_16+PIN_15 (qualification/pad_pair_pin16_pin15.v, image sha256 125ab36757d26102e36f932dcb45d191bdcac841dabaddbab736422ad8b63aa3, 34 pips): GP2 = 3,187,127 Hz (187,964 edges) and GP6 = 3,188,253 Hz (187,973 edges). PIN_15 ONLY (qualification/pad_only_pin15.v, sha256 612f853f48d5dc978e8027057a9b14c0388e68c92010495bea5f790015675ba5, 10 pips): GP2 = 3,187,733 Hz, GP6 = 0. PIN_16 ONLY (retained control image, sha256 40309ef7095a11ff6bd3efdf6d5a0e77942e39633e6f76863281dc8696621f7f): GP2 = 0, GP6 = 3,194,738 Hz. Neighbouring observed pads GP8 (PIN_18), GP5 (PIN_14), GP3 (PIN_13) and GP7 (PIN_17) read 0 edges in all three images. The productionized PIN_15 build, with no environment ban and the composition pinned only by chipdb/pad_output_qualified_L48.csv, is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the measured image.
scope: Three pads, L48, research-unsafe profile. The Python-architecture PCF placer composes AGAMEMNON_SOFT_PREFER, AGAMEMNON_SOFT_PENALTY and AGAMEMNON_NO_FFBRIDGE, which are registered experimental, so release-strict rejects these builds; the gate is not specific to pads. PIN_15 was chosen because the production graph admits exactly ONE feeder into its slot (RMUX16), so the router cannot silently reach it through an unmeasured feeder. PIN_18 is deliberately NOT the pairing partner: its pad-feed codeword writes eight bits at (18,13), which is PIN_15's config tile, and one of them is one of PIN_15's own two codeword bits. Rates are aliased by the Pico's polled edge counter, so they index 'toggling at SYSCLK/2' rather than an absolute frequency.

observed: All images FCB-accepted at 0x000f0002 and emitted with zero unmapped, predicted, or legacy-absolute selectors. PIN_14 ONLY: Pico GP5 30,569 edges / about 518,417 Hz; GP2/GP3/GP6/GP7/GP8 all 0. PIN_16+PIN_14 PAIR: GP5 28,585 edges / about 484,952 Hz and GP6 185,657 edges / about 3,149,505 Hz simultaneously; GP2/GP3/GP7/GP8 all 0. Fresh PIN_16 ONLY control: GP6 185,748 edges / about 3,150,621 Hz; GP2/GP3/GP5/GP7/GP8 all 0. Rates are Pico polling aliases and establish activity/independence, not absolute fabric frequency.
route: PIN_14 is physical decimal L48 lead 14, pad (19,13,z2), Pico GP5. Exact tail: X14Y9_SLICE15 F -> OMUX45 -> X15Y9_RMUX74 -> X19Y9_RMUX19 -> X19Y13_RMUX24 -> IOMUX02. The measured pad-feed hop is CFG_RMUX3[0,4]@(18,13), cells 408:0x40 and 524:0x80; the image verifier decoded IOMUX slot 2 to RMUX24, unparked.
root_cause: The exact feed hop already existed in the main RRG. The supplemental pad loader treated that duplicate feed as a duplicate ROW and continued before adding the row's distinct RMUX24->IOMUX02 terminal, making the exact composition unroutable. The loader now conditionally adds the feed but always processes the terminal.
reproducibility: The measured candidate used AGAMEMNON_VENDOR_OUT_SLICE=14,9,15. The qualified composition table now records that slice and the ordinary CLI derives it from the PCF. No-extra-environment production rebuilds of both the single and pair are byte-identical to the measured images.
consequence: The qualified top-edge output surface is now exactly four decimal L48 package leads: PIN_18, PIN_16, PIN_15 and PIN_14. PIN_14 is the third independently driven slot on shared pad tile (19,13), and it composes with PIN_16 without interference. This is not the ten-pad ring; PIN_10, PIN_11, PIN_12, PIN_13, PIN_17 and PIN_19 remain unqualified.
next_experiment: PIN_13 is the best fifth-pad discriminator: expose its RMUX08 terminal and reuse the already silicon-qualified PIN_16 RMUX55@(19,9)->RMUX08 hop, then repeat the single/pair/independence matrix. Separately, the direct PIN_25-input to PIN_18-output witness can retry blocked edge index 7 without any source-FF clock ambiguity.

observed: All builds used the ordinary CLI, emitted zero unmapped, predicted or legacy-absolute selectors, and the pair FCB-accepted at 0x000f0002 with sentinel 0xc0ffee02.
